Paragraph: "Whenever there is a decline in righteousness and an increase in unrighteousness, O Arjuna, at that time I manifest myself on earth." (Chapter 4, Verse 7) This famous verse explains Krishna's divine incarnation principle, demonstrating how the divine intervenes to restore cosmic balance and protect dharma in times of moral crisis.
Situation/Problem_Faced: A breakdown of moral order, cosmic imbalance, and widespread ethical decline (rise of adharma) creating societal and spiritual crisis.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: The Divine commits to active intervention (Avatara principle) by taking form on earth to restore righteousness and protect moral order when human effort alone is overwhelmed by moral degradation.
Outcome/Resolution: Restoration of cosmic balance, protection of dharma, and reassurance to humanity that moral crisis will be met with divine guidance and intervention.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Stress Management: Existential coping, Dealing with systemic crisis
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Fear: Anxiety over evil, Apprehension of chaos

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Dharma (Cosmic, moral, and ethical law maintaining balance)
Susthiti (Restoration of stability and spiritual equilibrium)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Krishna articulates the Avatara doctrine—a fundamental Hindu concept that divine grace actively descends to safeguard Dharma when systemic adharma threatens existence, providing ultimate spiritual protection and order.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Psychologically, this verse provides a narrative of ultimate support and cognitive reframing during existential anxiety. It mitigates feelings of helplessness in the face of widespread crisis by offering an anchor of hope, reassurance, and belief in an overarching order.
